Package common.core.subsystems

package common.core.subsystems
Mechanisms: the parts of a robot that motors move, like elevators, arms and rollers.

Pick the one that matches how it moves

  • LinearMechanism: moves in a straight line to a position. Elevators, sliders, telescopes.
  • PivotMechanism: rotates to an angle. Arms, wrists, shooter hoods, turrets.
  • RollerMechanism: spins, either just on and off or at a set speed. Intakes, hoppers, kickers, shooter flywheels.
All three are built on MechanismBase, which has everything they share: setpoints, running open loop, resetting, logging and Shuffleboard tuning.

Units

You pick a mechanism's units with its MotorConfig: meters for an elevator, degrees for an arm, rotations per second for a flywheel. Setpoints, measurements, tolerances and gains are then all in those units, and converting to the motor's own units is done for you.

Gains

Every mechanism with a setpoint takes a PIDFFConfig, which explains what each gain does. The control loop runs on the motor controller, 1000 times a second, so even fast mechanisms stay smooth.

Starting position

Motor encoders don't know where a mechanism is when the robot turns on. Each mechanism assumes it starts at a known position, usually against a hard stop. If something slips, push it back against the stop and call reset().

Mechanisms on mechanisms

setParent(...) mounts one mechanism on another, like a wrist on an arm or an arm on an elevator. Their 3D poses then move together in AdvantageScope, and gravity is worked out from the whole stack, e.g. a wrist's from the arm's angle plus its own. A mechanism's mass should include everything mounted on it.

Simulation

Each mechanism gives its motor a physics model, so it moves realistically in simulation with no changes to robot code. The mass, length and motor type passed to the constructor are what the model uses.
  • Class
    Description
    LinearMechanism
    Moves in a straight line to a position and holds it, at any incline: sliders (0 degrees), elevators (90 degrees), or anything in between.
    MechanismBase
    What every mechanism has in common: one or more motors, driven to a setpoint, with logging, Shuffleboard tuning widgets and a safety timeout.
    PivotMechanism
    Rotates to an angle and holds it: arms, wrists, shooter hoods, turrets.
    PivotMechanism.Orientation
    Which way the mechanism points at 0, and so the axis it rotates about.
    RollerMechanism
    Something that spins: intakes, hoppers, kickers, shooter flywheels.
    RollerMechanism.VelocityControl
    How a velocity-controlled roller works out its output.
